html:
The Hukuru Miskiy, or Old Friday Mosque, is the oldest standing mosque in Male, the capital of the Maldives, built in 1658 under Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar I.

It stands on the site of earlier mosques going back to the islands' conversion to Islam. Its walls are of coral stone, cut and fitted without mortar and carved with Quranic verses and patterns. Inside are lacquered wood panels and carved screens. Next to it stands a round minaret of the 1670s.

Coral-stone mosques like it once stood on many islands, a building tradition found nowhere else. It was the main Friday mosque until the larger Islamic Centre opened in 1984, and the coral-stone mosques are on the UNESCO tentative list for World Heritage.
sum: The Hukuru Miskiy, or Old Friday Mosque, is the oldest standing mosque in Male, the capital of the Maldives, built in 1658 under Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar I.
